recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR core. If the concept should be restored for implementers, handle that separately in the relevant additional-resource or extension-pack process, including deciding whether the extension should target Citation or DocumentReference.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive with Modification Jira asked why SubstanceSpecification/SubstanceDefinition used the name source for supporting literature and resolved to rename the attribute to informationSource and change its target from DocumentReference to Citation.
initial_application: Commits 0843635693167b180dacb358114b3257715f78c3 and 08d35148dd0fa3866502882e1805fe34cb107da4 applied the request by changing SubstanceDefinition.source to SubstanceDefinition.informationSource and changing the target profile from DocumentReference to Citation. BR&R 2022 WGM minutes also record the change as applied with a 13-0-0 vote.
additional_context: SubstanceDefinition remains in current build scope through source/fhir.ini, but the top-level informationSource element is now commented out in source/substancedefinition/structuredefinition-SubstanceDefinition.xml. Citation is no longer an active core resource, and commit 71567db3ee039ac6977be5f96a7e013896569a36 removed Citation from core while commenting out the Citation-targeted informationSource element. A later Zulip committers thread says the concept becomes extension/additional-resource follow-up territory after Citation moved out.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit and made no source changes. The current core source does not expose the old top-level source name, and reactivating or retargeting the inactive informationSource concept would be a new extension/additional-resource decision rather than required FHIR-31825 reconciliation.
